answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a costly identity bond. Each agent must lock a stake before it can join, and that stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Because one operator cannot cheaply fund thousands of locked stakes, spinning up fake agents to farm rewards stops paying off. Think of a mesa where every visitor must leave a deposit, and the path back down basalt ridges keeps the crowd honest. Agents that wander off to spawn clones lose more than they gain.
